summary: Sega's blue-sky driving series, from Yu Suzuki's 1986 arcade landmark through Master System spin-offs, OutRunners, OutRun 2, Coast 2 Coast, and the delisted HD Online Arcade release.

entries.title: Out Run
entries.definitive_edition: Sega Ages Out Run on Nintendo Switch

emulation.emulator: Native Switch / original arcade hardware / platform-specific emulators for secondary ports
emulation.notes: Use Sega Ages Switch for the main route; use Genesis and 3DS only for unique extras.

primary.why: The 1986 arcade game received many home ports and later Sega Ages/3D Classics releases. Sega Ages on Switch is the best current official route to the arcade game, with modern presentation and the corrected audio used in later re-releases; the Genesis/Mega Drive and 3DS versions remain secondary for their unique extras.
primary.how_to_play: Play Sega Ages Out Run on Nintendo Switch. Sample the Genesis/Mega Drive version for its exclusive music track and 3D Out Run on Nintendo 3DS for stereoscopic presentation.

secondary.exclusive_content: Exclusive music track Step On Beat
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Mega Drive/Genesis port's soundtrack option.
secondary.why: It is lower fidelity than the arcade/Sega Ages route but has a documented exclusive track.

secondary.what_to_play: Sample the 3DS release for the stereoscopic version.
secondary.why: The 3DS version is not the main current route, but its 3D presentation is unique.

entries.remaster_caveats: Some older ports differ heavily from the arcade game; use them as historical curiosities rather than the main route.

entries.title: OutRun 3-D

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 3DS hardware / Master System emulator fallback
emulation.notes: Original Master System requires Sega 3-D glasses for the intended effect.

primary.why: OutRun 3-D is a distinct Master System game built for Sega's stereoscopic glasses, later ported to Nintendo 3DS as part of Sega 3D Reprint Archives. The 3DS release is the best official way to preserve the stereoscopic concept.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Sega 3D Reprint Archives on Nintendo 3DS; use Master System hardware with 3-D glasses for original authenticity.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a 3D version of the original arcade Out Run; it is a separate Master System game.

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / arcade preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use arcade route for the main playthrough.

primary.why: Turbo OutRun is the arcade follow-up to Out Run and was ported to several computers plus FM Towns and Mega Drive. No modern definitive release or exclusive home content is documented, so the arcade version is the fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or through a legal arcade-preservation setup; use FM Towns/Mega Drive only as historical home routes.

emulation.notes: Use Master System emulation for capture-friendly play.

primary.why: Battle Out Run is a Master System-only Out Run spin-off with Chase H.Q.-style car-ramming objectives and upgrades. With no other platform documented, Master System is the only route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Master System hardware or a compatible emulator.

emulation.notes: Use Amiga emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Out Run Europa is a Probe/U.S. Gold spin-off across European computers plus Game Gear and Master System. With no arcade original and no platform-exclusive content documented, Amiga is the selected 16-bit home-computer route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Amiga version through original hardware or accurate Amiga emulation; Master System/Game Gear are fallback console/handheld routes.

emulation.notes: Use accurate Genesis emulation or original hardware.

primary.why: OutRun 2019 is a Genesis/Mega Drive pseudo-sequel with futuristic routes and a rocket-boosted car. The 2005 Play TV Legends release is a plug-and-play reissue, but the original console version is the full primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Mega Drive/Genesis release on original hardware or through a compatible emulator.

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / MAME-compatible preservation setup
emulation.notes: Linked cabinet play is the ideal route when available.

primary.why: OutRunners restored the route-forking, lighthearted Out Run feel in arcades and was later ported to Genesis/Mega Drive. The arcade version supports linked multiplayer and is the fidelity/feature route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original linked arcade cabinets where possible, or through a legal arcade-preservation setup; use Genesis only as a compromised home port.

entries.title: OutRun 2

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or verify xemu compatibility; online features require replacement-service support.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox 480p output or Xbox emulation

primary.why: OutRun 2 launched in arcades and came to Xbox with 480p anamorphic widescreen, home challenge modes, Xbox Live support, unlockable Scud Race/Daytona USA 2 tracks, extra cars/music, and the original Out Run. For this specific entry, Xbox is more complete than the arcade version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or a compatible Xbox emulator; Insignia can restore some original-Xbox online functionality where supported.

entries.remaster_caveats: OutRun 2006 includes OutRun 2 SP content but omits some Xbox OutRun 2 bonus content; treat it as a separate entry.

entries.title: OutRun 2 SP / SP DX
entries.definitive_edition: OutRun 2 SP DX / SDX arcade release

emulation.emulator: Original arcade hardware / Lindbergh preservation setup
emulation.notes: Use the arcade cabinet for the intended co-op hardware experience.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sega Lindbergh SP DX/SDX cabinet fidelity

primary.version: OutRun 2 SP DX / SDX arcade release
primary.why: OutRun 2 SP added 15 new courses, and SP DX/SDX later moved to Sega Lindbergh hardware with higher resolution and cooperative Ferrari-cabinet play. For the arcade update itself, SP DX/SDX is the highest-fidelity cabinet route; the content also appears in OutRun 2006.
primary.how_to_play: Play an SP DX/SDX arcade cabinet for the cabinet/co-op experience, or use OutRun 2006 for a home version of much of the SP content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Home SP content is covered by OutRun 2006: Coast 2 Coast.

entries.title: OutRun 2006: Coast 2 Coast
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release plus PSP/Japanese PS2 supplements

emulation.emulator: Native PC / PPSSPP for PSP supplement / PCSX2 for PS2 supplement
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main route; use PSP/PS2 only for documented content differences.

primary.why: Coast 2 Coast combines an OutRun 2 SP conversion with a career-style Coast 2 Coast mode and shipped on Xbox, PS2, PSP, and Windows. Windows is the fidelity route, but the PSP version has a different mission set and the PS2/PSP link/Japanese PS2 unlock handling creates a completeness caveat.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release if already owned; preserve PSP separately for its different mission set and use Japanese PS2 only if you want the unlocks available without PS2/PSP linking.

secondary.exclusive_content: Different mission set from the console/PC versions
secondary.what_to_play: Play/sample the PSP missions that differ from the main Windows route.
secondary.why: The PSP release is lower fidelity but has documented system-specific mission content.

secondary.exclusive_content: PSP-linked unlockables are included from the start because PSP connectivity was removed
secondary.what_to_play: Use only if preserving the Japanese PS2 unlock state matters.
secondary.why: It is a completeness convenience, not the fidelity route.

entries.remaster_caveats: The game is delisted/unavailable in many storefront contexts due to Ferrari licensing history; preserve legitimate copies.

entries.title: OutRun Online Arcade
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360 XBLA release if already owned

emulation.notes: No legitimate new-purchase route is documented; play only if already owned.

primary.why: OutRun Online Arcade is an HD, online-focused adaptation of the OutRun 2 line with reduced content versus OutRun 2006, released on XBLA and European PSN before Ferrari-license delisting. The Xbox 360 version is the broader primary route if already owned; PS3 is Europe-only.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 if the XBLA license is already on the account/console; European PS3 owners can use the PSN version if already purchased.

entries.remaster_caveats: Delisted from PSN/XBLA after the Ferrari contract expired; it is not a replacement for the fuller OutRun 2006 package.
